title: Coordinated regional pin reconciliation and probabilistic canary split enforcement
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When customers perform canary or A/B rollouts with both model version pinning and region/tier preferences enabled, the current route-resolver can produce inconsistent exposure and capacity hotspots. Examples observed: 1) a small fraction of sessions pinned to a canary variant in a low-capacity region cause repeated fallbacks to higher-tier variants, amplifying traffic against a few nodes; 2) probabilistic canary splits applied at request-time get bypassed by long-lived client pins, blocking measured rollout velocity and skewing metrics.

Goal: Implement a reconciliation layer that deterministically combines three inputs — persistent pins (session/customer), runtime routing policies (region, tier), and rollout-level probabilistic splits — so that: a) canary exposure matches intended split across regions and tiers; b) pins gracefully decay or graduate to rollout policy; c) fallback ordering to compatible model variants is predictable and capacity-aware.

Scope: Route-resolver changes, pin metadata schema update, rollout-controller tweaks, metrics/experiment harness, and integration tests simulating heterogenous capacity across regions and model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic routing result for identical request contexts (session id, customer id, route config) across 95% of simulated runs
Canary exposure aligns with configured global split +-5% when measured across regions with skewed capacity
Pins have TTL and a graduation policy: pins older than configurable threshold either decay probabilistically or inherit rollout assignment according to policy
Fallback variant ordering respects region tier preferences and avoids amplifying load on the same physical hosts where possible
E2E integration tests that reproduce the two failure modes described in the problem section are added to CI
implementation_notes: Add pin metadata: {origin, created_at, ttl_seconds, affinity_hash} stored in pin-store (key: customer:{id}:pin) — lightweight schema change; pins remain server-side only

Introduce reconciliation function in route-resolver with the following pipeline: 1) gather inputs (pin, route policy, rollout state, per-region capacity snapshot) 2) apply deterministic seed ordering using affinity_hash to decide deterministic vs probabilistic outcome 3) apply TTL/graduation rules 4) compute final candidate list and order by cost+latency+compatibility 5) apply final gating (capacity thresholds) before selecting node/variant

Probabilistic canary enforcement: use two-tier split model. First apply global rollout split at cohort assignment (based on stable hash of customer id + route id). Then apply request-level sampling only if cohort assignment is undecided or for shadowed experiments.

Routing fallback: introduce per-variant cost vector (latency_est, token_cost, capacity_pressure_score) to compute a composite score used to order fallbacks so that variants in the same region but different tier are preferred over cross-region fallbacks when latency budget allows
Telemetry: emit routing_decision events with fields: resolver_version, pin_state, cohort_assignment, chosen_variant, fallback_candidates, capacity_snapshot_hash
Testing harness: augment existing integration tests with a topology simulator that can simulate regional capacity loss and variable shard packing to validate fallback ordering and hotspot avoidance
decisions: Use server-side pins with TTL instead of extending client-managed tokens to avoid client drift and simplify revocation
Deterministic cohort assignment uses SHA256(customer_id + route_id) mod 10000 to generate a stable percentile for rollout splits
Pins older than 'pin_grace_seconds' enter probabilistic decay where each request has configurable chance to ignore pin and follow rollout cohort
Route-resolver will surface a candidate scoring API consumed by orchestrator for final allocation; this keeps scoring logic testable and pluggable
risks: If capacity snapshot is stale, fallback decisions might still concentrate load on unlucky nodes — mitigate by conservative thresholds and fast refresh for high-pressure routes
Changing pin semantics may upset customers with expectations of strict pinning — add migration path and admin toggle per-tenant
Additional route-resolver CPU work could increase latency for high-QPS endpoints — will gate behind feature flag and measure overhead in canary
